lab_indicators_24h.note: National aggregate: Ituri 167 samples documented in the collection network / 70 positive (47 living, 23 deaths) = 41.9%; Nord-Kivu 105 analyzed / 9 positive (8 living, 1 death) = 8.6%. Positivity uses 79 positives over 272 analyzed samples (Ituri + Nord-Kivu). Haut-Uele's 4 collected samples are still in analysis, carry no positivity and are excluded from the analyzed denominator; they must NOT be read as pending positives. The day's laboratory positives (70 + 9 = 79) EQUAL the day's confirmations exactly, as at SitRep65. Ituri's apparent positivity rose to 41.9% on an unchanged 167-sample documented denominator, a test-targeting movement rather than a measured prevalence change.

care_continuity: SitRep66 Tableau 6: 734 in isolation at end of day (295 confirmed / 439 suspected, a split that closes exactly against the census) at 78.2% global bed occupancy (734/939 beds); Ituri 69.3% (553/798) after a bed expansion from 706, Nord-Kivu 128.4% (181/141) and saturated; Haut-Uele and Tshopo report ND. The bed identity closes exactly at every level (720 J-1 + 108 admissions - 94 exits = 734; Ituri 543 + 70 - 60 = 553; Nord-Kivu 177 + 38 - 34 = 181). Exits over 24h (94 total): 18 deaths, 63 non-cases, 3 recoveries, 10 escapes. Ituri first-line personnel: 121 cumulative infections, 67 recovered (Table 8; the prose says 65), 18 hospitalized, 36 deaths (CFR 29.8%).

Recovered advanced only marginally to 469 DRC cumulative (+3, all in Ituri), against 18 deaths and 63 non-case exits over the same 24 hours. Country-scope recovered 480 (+11 Uganda anchor). A recovery count that low beside the isolation throughput is a case-management signal worth watching rather than a data artifact this cycle.
highlights: A NEW health zone was affected: Adja, in Aru Territory, northern Ituri, entering the table at 10 confirmed cases and 1 death in a single cycle rather than as one index case. That takes Ituri to 28/36 and the national roster to 47 zones touched, 46 actively transmitting. A zone that appears at 10 cases was already carrying an established chain when it was detected, so the figure is a floor on what has been happening there, not this cycle's incidence.

79 new confirmed cases (Ituri 70, Nord-Kivu 9) and 37 new deaths (Ituri 35, Nord-Kivu 2) take the DRC cumulative cleanly to 2423 confirmed / 967 deaths (CFR 39.9%) with no harmonization this cycle. Ituri's new cases concentrate at Bunia (18), Nizi (16), Rwampara (10) and the new Adja (10). Laboratory positives (70 + 9 = 79) equal the day's confirmations exactly.

Surveillance capacity fell on both axes even as the case count held: contact follow-up dropped to 81.1% (8531/10519) from 85.8%, and Ituri's alert-investigation rate to 75.6% (335/443) from 86.4%, leaving 108 alerts uninvestigated. Haut-Uele investigated 4 of 36 alerts. Both the contact cohort and the contacts seen shrank, and Tshopo stopped reporting contacts while Haut-Uele resumed, so the national coverage figure mixes performance with a change in who reports.

alerts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 3 (at 19/07): 1103 alerts of the day (993 new + 110 Report-J-1) across Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uele; Tshopo and Sud-Kivu report ND. Investigated 82.6% (911/1103): Ituri 75.6% (335/443), Nord-Kivu 91.7% (572/624), Haut-Uele 11.1% (4/36). Every column reconciles exactly: province rows sum to the national totals for alerts (1103), investigated (911), validated-living (174 = 154+19+1), validated-deceased (78 = 53+22+3) and suspects (252 = 207+41+4), and the J-1/new split closes (110 + 993 = 1103). Validated suspects 252 = 174 living + 78 community deaths under investigation. Ituri's investigation rate fell to 75.6% from 86.4% with 108 alerts left uninvestigated, and Haut-Uele carried 32 of its 36 alerts as J-1 backlog while investigating only 4.

challenges.finding: A new health zone, Adja (Ituri, Aru Territory), was reported affected and entered the table at 10 confirmed cases / 1 death at once rather than as a single index case, indicating the chain was already established when detected. The national roster moves to 47 zones touched, 46 actively transmitting.
challenges.response: Deploy investigation, contact-listing and IPC capacity to Adja and reassess the northern Ituri axis toward the Uganda and South Sudan borders.

challenges.finding: Reticence toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.
challenges.response: Intensify CREC/RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams, and increase the number of EDS teams.

challenges.finding: Contact-tracing performance fell to 81.1% nationally (Ituri 81.3%, Nord-Kivu 83.8%, Haut-Uele 52.3%), below the 95% threshold, with both the cohort and the number seen shrinking.
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision, and investigate the drop in Ituri and Haut-Uele.

challenges.finding: Ituri investigated only 75.6% of its 443 alerts (108 uninvestigated) and Haut-Uele 11.1% of 36, of which 32 were carried forward as a J-1 backlog.
challenges.response: Clear the alert-investigation backlog and restore daily investigation capacity in Ituri and Haut-Uele.

challenges.finding: Nord-Kivu isolation occupancy is saturated at 128.4% (181 patients for 141 beds) while Ituri fell to 69.3% (553 for 798) after a bed expansion; Haut-Uele and Tshopo did not report capacity.
challenges.response: Expand Nord-Kivu CTE/CT capacity and restore systematic bed-capacity reporting in Haut-Uele and Tshopo.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs and limited functional triage units carry a high nosocomial-infection risk against 121 cumulative first-line personnel infections including 36 deaths (CFR 29.8%).
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforced IPC training.

challenges.finding: Geographic extension with high mobility carries urban, riverine and cross-border diffusion risk, now including the new northern-Ituri zone Adja.
challenges.response: Reinforce cross-border coordination, including the joint DRC/Uganda technical evaluation of the Kasenyi mobile laboratory.

challenges.finding: Decentralized proximity laboratories are still being deployed, leaving long confirmation delays and undetected transmission.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralized diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across the response pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilization and advocacy with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential health services (CEHS) is compromised, raising indirect non-Ebola mortality.
challenges.response: Effective implementation of free care and reinforcement of CEHS.

challenges.finding: Frontline provider payment remains a recurring interruption risk to response activities including dignified and secure burials.
challenges.response: Regularize provider payment and secure dedicated financing.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 4 (19 July): 10519 under follow-up, 8531 seen, 81.1% national, below the 95% operational threshold and down from SitRep65's 85.8%. Province rows: Ituri 81.3% (6167/7581), Nord-Kivu 83.8% (2202/2628), Haut-Uele 52.3% (162/310); Tshopo reports ND and Sud-Kivu follow-up is closed (0/0, NA). The province rows sum EXACTLY to the national totals (7581+2628+310 = 10519 under follow-up; 6167+2202+162 = 8531 seen) and the cover KPI agrees, so no rate cluster is in conflict. BOTH sides of the ratio fell this cycle: the denominator dropped 12251 -> 10519 (-1732) and contacts seen dropped 10517 -> 8531 (-1986), so coverage fell despite a smaller cohort. Tshopo went from 78/78 = 100.0% at SitRep65 to ND, while Haut-Uele returned to the table at 52.3% after reporting ND last cycle; the national movement is therefore partly a change in which provinces report, not only a change in performance.

patient_movement_total.data_gap_note: SitRep66 Tableau 6 end-of-day census 734 at 78.2% occupancy (734/939 beds): Ituri 553 @69.3% (798 beds, 275 confirmed / 278 suspected), Nord-Kivu 181 @128.4% (141 beds, 20 / 161); Haut-Uele and Tshopo report ND. The confirmed/suspect split CLOSES exactly (295 + 439 = 734, and each province closes: Ituri 275+278 = 553, Nord-Kivu 20+161 = 181). The bed identity also closes exactly at every level: national 720 J-1 + 108 admissions - 94 exits = 734; Ituri 543 + 70 - 60 = 553; Nord-Kivu 177 + 38 - 34 = 181. Exits over 24h (94 total): 18 deaths, 63 non-cases, 3 recoveries, 10 escapes, 0 HGR transfers. Nord-Kivu's 128.4% is arithmetically consistent with 181/141 this cycle, unlike SitRep65's printed 123.1%. Ituri bed capacity expanded 706 -> 798, dropping its occupancy to 69.3%. The section-4 prose says Ituri has '539 malades en isolement' while giving 275 confirmed + 278 suspects (= 553) in the same sentence; Tableau 6 and the cover both print 553 and 553/798 = 69.3% matches the printed occupancy, so 539 is a prose typo (see preserved_conflicts).

poe_poc_combined_ituri_nord_kivu.scope_note: SitRep66 reports PoE/PoC as a combined Ituri + Nord-Kivu block (75 points: Ituri 60, Nord-Kivu 15), carried under a combined key and NOT under poe_poc_ituri; no Ituri-only split is published and none is inferred. All 8 notified alerts and the single intercepted body were in Ituri; 100% of validated living alerts were referred to a CT/CTE.

priorities.priority: Stand up investigation, contact listing and IPC in Adja (Ituri), which entered the roster at 10 confirmed / 1 death rather than a single index case, and reassess the northern Ituri axis toward the Uganda and South Sudan borders.

Reverse the contact-follow-up fall to 81.1% (Ituri 81.3%, Haut-Uele 52.3%) and clear the alert-investigation backlog (Ituri 75.6% with 108 uninvestigated; Haut-Uele 11.1% of 36, 32 of them carried from J-1).
Relieve Nord-Kivu isolation saturation at 128.4% (181 of 141 beds) and restore bed-capacity reporting in Haut-Uele and Tshopo, both ND this cycle.
Complete the joint DRC/Uganda technical evaluation of the Kasenyi mobile laboratory and sustain screening across the 75 combined Ituri + Nord-Kivu PoE/PoC that registered 162309 travellers.
Sustain residual epidemiological surveillance in Sud-Kivu, where Miti-Murhesa remains outside the active-transmission set, toward a provincial end-of-outbreak declaration.

preserved_conflicts: SitRep66 national headline is DRC-only (2423 confirmed / 967 confirmed deaths across five provinces); the country-scope snapshot adds the Uganda component (20/2/11) separately -> 2443 confirmed / 969 deaths / 480 recovered. The Uganda MoH API became reachable again this cycle and reports no new Uganda cases through 2026-07-20, so the anchor is carried unchanged on a confirmed rather than an assumed basis; the prior Cloudflare 522 failures were transient availability, not a data revision.

NEW AFFECTED HEALTH ZONE: Adja (Ituri, Aru Territory) enters the roster at 10 confirmed / 1 death in a single cycle rather than as one index case, taking Ituri 27/36 -> 28/36 and the national count 46 -> 47 touched (46 actively transmitting). A zone appearing at 10 cases indicates an already-established chain detected late, so its first-cycle figure is a floor, not an incidence estimate. Adja is rendered at its own GRID3 v8.0 area-weighted polygon centroid and is never collapsed into a neighbouring zone.

Ituri isolation census: Tableau 6 and the cover print 553, and the section-4 prose gives 275 confirmed + 278 suspected in the same sentence (= 553) while stating '539 malades en isolement'. 553 is promoted (it closes the province split, the national census 295 + 439 = 734, and the printed 69.3% = 553/798); the 539 is preserved as a prose typo.

First-line personnel (PPL): Tableau 8 totals 121 cases / 67 recovered / 18 hospitalized / 36 deaths, and its ten zone rows sum exactly to each of those figures. The response-pillar prose gives 65 recovered against the same 121/18/36. Table 8's 67 is promoted as the internally consistent value and the prose 65 preserved.

Contact-tracing coverage fell to 81.1% (8531/10519) from 85.8%, with BOTH sides of the ratio falling: the cohort under follow-up dropped 12251 -> 10519 (-1732) and contacts seen dropped 10517 -> 8531 (-1986). Reporting composition also changed: Tshopo reported 78/78 = 100.0% at SitRep65 and ND here, while Haut-Uele returned at 52.3% (162/310) after ND last cycle. The national movement is therefore partly a change in which provinces report and must not be read as a pure performance change. Province rows still sum exactly to the national totals.

Haut-Uele has 4 laboratory samples in analysis and reported no new confirmed cases or deaths; these must NOT be treated as pending positives. Its province row holds at 16 confirmed / 10 deaths, unchanged after the SitRep65 harmonization.

Ituri's alert-investigation rate fell to 75.6% (335/443) from 86.4%, leaving 108 alerts uninvestigated, and Haut-Uele investigated 4 of 36 (11.1%) with 32 carried forward as a J-1 backlog. Every Tableau-3 column nonetheless reconciles exactly, so this is a measured capacity movement rather than a reporting artifact.

ECDC and WHO remain secondary and lagging for this cycle: ECDC is still aligned to SitRep65 values and WHO DON613 / WHO AFRO report 09 trail the INSP series. INSP SitRep66 is the promoted primary and must not be overridden by those lagging secondary sources.

The cover per-province CFR line (Ituri 37.5%, Nord-Kivu 59.0%, Sud-Kivu 33.3%, Haut-Uele 62.5%, Tshopo 80.0%) agrees with Table 1 for all five provinces (811/2160 = 37.5%; 141/239 = 59.0%; 1/3 = 33.3%; 10/16 = 62.5%; 4/5 = 80.0%).
